title: POC scoping: Acme Healthcare - quality eval plan
summary: SE-led scoping to define success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and a quality evaluation plan (golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks, scoring). Agreed next steps: Redwood to share eval spreadsheet, schedule benchmark run, provide security docs and pricing. Target pilot in 4 weeks.
success_criteria: <25% hallucination rate on clinical summarization v1
99th percentile latency < 500ms for single-turn prompts in hosted mode
Model regression delta <= 1.5% relative to golden baseline across scoring metrics
benchmarks_goals: peak concurrency 40 qps during simulated clinic hours
end-to-end latencies (p95) under 750ms for multi-turn flows
run 5k golden prompts across dataset for quality measurement
next_steps: Jordan Lee: Share quality-eval spreadsheet (golden prompts + scoring rubric) by 2025-05-14
Priya Nair: Schedule benchmark run and provide test harness instructions by 2025-05-16
Acme team (Maya): Provide 100 golden prompts and 500 regression examples by 2025-05-19
Jordan: Share SOC2 and network architecture whitepaper + on-prem checklist by 2025-05-15
All: Follow-up sync to review benchmark results week of 2025-05-26
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share pricing and dedicated capacity options by 2025-05-16
Priya Nair: Prep Dockerized benchmark harness and send access instructions by 2025-05-16
Maya Chen: Export 500 anonymized past notes for regression testing by 2025-05-19
Luis Gomez: Send list of required compliance artifacts and SSO details by 2025-05-15
transcript: 00:00 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll kick off on time. Today the goal is to scope the POC for quality evaluation, we want to nail down success criteria, workloads and timelines. 00:22 Speaker 2 (Samir): Thanks Jordan, appreciate it. Quick background: we're looking to automate clinical note summarization and triage for the e-visit flow. Key concerns are hallucination and strict format output for downstream EHR ingestion. 00:40 Speaker 3 (Maya): yes, and we have latency constraints because notes need to appear in the workflow within a couple seconds ideally, and security is obviously critical. 00:52 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Totally. Priya from our SE team will walk through the evaluation plan and benchmarks. Priya? 01:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): Hi all. I'll start with the high-level approach: 1) define golden prompts and golden outputs for critical use cases, 2) run regression tests on historical anonymized notes, 3) measure hallucination/format violations via heuristics and manual spot checks, 4) compute composite scoring for pass/fail per prompt. 01:35 Speaker 2 (Samir): When you say golden prompts, do you mean we craft canonical prompts and canonical expected outputs? 01:43 Speaker 4 (Priya): Yes, exactly. We'll collect about 100 golden prompts from you that represent the most sensitive flows — discharge summaries, medication reconciliation, HPI summaries. For each prompt we want a golden output or a set of acceptable variants. 02:00 Speaker 3 (Maya): We can do that. We'll anonymize and give you samples. How do you score hallucinations? 02:08 Speaker 4 (Priya): We use a combination — automated string checks to detect extraneous medical entities not present in input, regex/format checks for required fields (e.g., "MedList:" block), and a spot-check rubric where humans label a small subset for false positives/negatives. Scoring: per example we compute precision/recall for extracted entities and a binary format pass/fail; then we aggregate into a weighted composite score. 02:36 Speaker 5 (Luis): For security, we need to know data retention and whether PII will be stored on Redwood-hosted temp storage during benchmarks. 02:45 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll send the security docs — our default is ephemeral storage for hosted runs; for Dedicated or Private options we can keep everything in your VPC. Jordan: action note to include SOC2 and KMS details. 02:58 Speaker 5 (Luis): Good. Also SSO and audit log capability? 03:03 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Yes, SAML/SSO supported, audit logs available in Console. We'll include specifics. 03:10 Speaker 4 (Priya): Back to the eval plan: regression testing — we'll run your 500 historical notes through the candidate model variants and compare to golden outputs for format/semantic drift. We'll flag regressions where composite score drops past threshold (we suggested 1.5% delta max). 03:30 Speaker 2 (Samir): What's the plan for latency benchmarking and request shaping? 03:36 Speaker 4 (Priya): We'll simulate 40 qps peak concurrency with same token distributions you see in production, but start with a 0-10 qps ramp to check stability. For latency we capture p50/p95/p99 and end-to-end including network and client-side processing. For hosted vs dedicated we can show both sets of profiles. 03:58 Speaker 3 (Maya): Token cost estimates? 04:02 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll provide unit economics for each model variant. Target is to keep cost below the number you mentioned, but we can show tradeoffs: larger model = better quality but higher cost/latency. 04:18 Speaker 4 (Priya): Regarding hallucination detection specifics — we'll use entity alignment: if the model outputs a medication or diagnosis not present in the source text, it counts as hallucination unless it's clearly inferred and part of the golden. We'll surface examples and ask human raters to adjudicate ambiguous cases. 04:36 Speaker 2 (Samir): That sounds reasonable. How do you define format compliance? 04:41 Speaker 4 (Priya): We codify required fields and regexes for blocks, e.g., MedList: each med must be on a new line with name, dose, frequency. We run deterministic checks first; any failures get human review to avoid false positives. 05:00 Speaker 3 (Maya): About datasets: we'll send 100 golden prompts + 500 anonymized notes. Is that enough? 05:07 Speaker 4 (Priya): It's a good start for POC. Ideally we want a stratified sample across note types. For benchmarks we prefer at least 5k examples if you want strong statistical confidence, but for initial quality gating 500 is fine. 05:23 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Timeline proposals? 05:25 Speaker 4 (Priya): Week 0: collect golden prompts and regression set (you). Week 1: Redwood runs initial eval and shares baseline scores and error examples. Week 2: joint review, iterate on prompts and scoring heuristics. Week 3: full benchmark run (5k) and latencies. Week 4: final report and recommendation — so about 4 weeks to pilot. 05:48 Speaker 2 (Samir): That aligns with our internal timeline. We need executive buy-in by end of month. 05:55 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Good; we'll aim for results prior to your exec meeting. 06:00 Speaker 3 (Maya): A quick question on model variants — will you test quantized versions or only base floats? 06:06 Speaker 4 (Priya): We'll test multiple profiles: float32 / int8 / int4 quantized candidates, and measure quality delta vs cost/latency. We also include a KV-cache warm start for multi-turn to reduce latency. 06:20 Speaker 5 (Luis): For Dedicated or Private, what changes in observability? We need token-level tracing and retention controls. 06:27 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools and you can keep logs in your VPC. We'll provide tracing hooks with sampling settings. 06:35 Speaker 2 (Samir): Any red flags from your side? 06:38 Speaker 4 (Priya): Only that we need the anonymized data sooner rather than later; also clear definition of format rules to avoid subjective scoring drift. 06:46 Speaker 3 (Maya): On hallucination tolerances, can we set different thresholds per note type? 06:50 Speaker 4 (Priya): Absolutely — discharge summaries might have a stricter threshold than triage notes. We'll encode per-type thresholds in the scoring config. 07:01 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Let's talk deliverables. We'll provide: 1) Quality-eval spreadsheet with golden prompts and scoring rubric, 2) benchmark harness + instructions, 3) security docs + SOC2, 4) cost model and model-variant comparison. 07:19 Speaker 2 (Samir): Great. Also please include sample transcripts of failure modes so our clinicians understand what to expect. 07:26 Speaker 4 (Priya): We'll annotate top 20 failures with suggested mitigations. 07:31 Speaker 3 (Maya): For the human labelling, what sample size do you recommend? 07:34 Speaker 4 (Priya): For spot checks, 200 examples labeled gives good signal; for adjudication of ambiguous hallucinations maybe another 100. We can support labeling through our CSM if you need. 07:47 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Pricing and dedicated capacity details will follow in email. 07:50 Speaker 2 (Samir): Any compliance issues with exporting anonymized notes to hosted Redwood for benchmarks? 07:55 Speaker 5 (Luis): We need to validate that anonymization meets HIPAA de-identification standards. 07:59 Speaker 1 (Jordan): We'll include our de-id guidance and options to run benchmarks in Private where data never leaves your network. 08:07 Speaker 3 (Maya): Ok next steps recap? 08:10 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Jordan to share eval spreadsheet and SOC2/KMS docs by 2025-05-14. Priya to schedule benchmark harness and run initial tests by 2025-05-16. Maya to deliver golden prompts + 500 anonymized notes by 2025-05-19. Follow-up sync week of 2025-05-26. 08:31 Speaker 2 (Samir): Sounds good. Thanks everyone. 08:33 Speaker 1 (Jordan): Thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the doc links. End of call.
final_recap: Agreed POC scope: build a quality evaluation over golden prompts + regression tests, run latency and concurrency benchmarks, and deliver a final report in ~4 weeks. Security options include hosted ephemeral runs or Dedicated/Private deployment for data residency. Next steps assigned and timelines set.
